entry.content:

Cineol-X 224 is a free reverb plugin for macOS and Windows that emulates classic hardware units using data derived from original Lexicon 224 v4.4 and 224 XL v8.21 firmware. It includes 28 programs spanning the six algorithms of the original 224 and 22 algorithms from the 224XL, featuring an automatic engine selection function.

Operation requires users to supply their own original Lexicon ROM files upon first use. The VST3 plugin is available for download via the project's GitHub releases page.

entry.title: M-Vave FM-1 Pocket Synthesizer Emerges as Custom Firmware Platform
entry.content:
Links: arstechnica.com | source | discussion

The M-Vave FM-1 is an inexpensive pocket frequency-modulation synthesizer that has evolved into a popular platform for community-developed custom firmware. Originally released as a budget device inspired by the Yamaha DX7, the hardware sparked reverse-engineering efforts that led to user-created software expanding its capabilities far beyond its stock configuration.

In response to the community trend, manufacturer M-Vave launched FM1 Open, an open-source development package featuring a browser-based workbench, software development kit, and updated firmware options. Community developers have since ported a wide variety of alternate packages to the device, transforming the pocket synthesizer into a multi-engine groovebox, chiptune workstation, and even a platform capable of running Doom.

entry.title: AudioBrain Releases ChimeBrain Physically Modeled Wind-Chime Instrument for macOS
entry.content:
Links: kvraudio.com | source

AudioBrain has released ChimeBrain, a physically modeled wind-chime instrument designed for macOS. Instead of relying on prerecorded samples, the software calculates the vibrations of suspended metal bars in real time to generate sound for music production, scoring, and sound design.

The instrument features up to 36 individually configurable metal bars with adjustable dimensions, materials, and pitch registers, alongside MIDI performance options, sweep and shake gestures, and direct on-screen interaction. It also includes five virtual microphone models and optional room acoustics, with version 1.0.2 disabling room reverb by default on new instances to reduce CPU usage. ChimeBrain is available as a universal AU, VST3, and standalone plugin priced at $19.

Major pop artists and record labels, including Taylor Swift and Ariana Grande, are increasingly utilizing the iTunes Store to release digital collectibles, bonus tracks, and limited editions. Years after subscription streaming became the dominant mode of music consumption, the legacy platform is seeing renewed activity driven by artists seeking to engage dedicated fanbases.

By encouraging superfans to purchase digital downloads, artists can effectively bolster their performance on official music sales and charts. This trend highlights how legacy digital storefronts continue to serve as strategic tools for direct monetization and chart optimization in the modern music industry.
